Module 1:  Agency, education and innovation (1 hour)
Voting for the ladder of power and freedom

Position of the majority of young [sex of FGD] on the ladder of power and freedom (private rating): 5 = Power and freedom to make almost all major life decisions: 4 votes; 4 = Power and freedom to make many major life decisions: 1 vote; 3 = Power and freedom to make some major life decisions: 2 votes; 2 = Only a small amount of power and freedom: 2 votes; 1 = Almost no power or freedom to make decisions: 0 votes
Step 5

As a married young men, I now have power and freedom to make almost all major decisions in my life because I am independent from my parents. I am now in charge of my own home. My parents have freed me to do whatever I want to do in my life.
Step 2
Some of the youth stay with step mothers who ill-treat them, so their power and freedom to make decisions is limited.
Many of the young men staying with their step mothers lost their mothers through death.
The step mother’s children are in a better position to take advantage of opportunities to lift themselves within the family than children of the deceased wife.
Young men staying with their step mothers are always blamed when something bad occurs. You might be able to do something that can earn you a living but support from other people is limited.
We have only a small amount of power and freedom because even if we think of an income generating project that may improve our wellbeing we lack the resources to start the project.
Going to school is good because it gives you knowledge which you can use in your life.

Parents must encourage their children to go to school but some of the parents are the main culprits for having their children out of school, or ending their education prematurely. Parents have a major role to play in educating children. Yet some parents are not committed to educating their children, because they do not value education themselves.

As children we have to know that education is important in our life because in this country people who are better off in life are those who have gone to school. Even if my parents do not send me to school I have the right to try by all means to make myself go to school.
Most youths are failing to attend school because they are orphans, they do not have someone to pay their school fees.
It is useful to get an education because
Education earns you a living. You will able to produce certificates when looking for a job and education builds your capacity to learn new things in life.

You appreciate the importance of presenting yourself properly in public, for example, dressing yourself appropriately. As a result you will be respected in the community. An educated person has a better understanding of the social and economic developments in the community and also in the country. If you are educated you are able to avoid conflicts with other people.
For you to make it in life you need to have gone to school. As we can see in our country, more and more people are getting educated, so there is increasing competition in the job market.

Even doing farming – which is our main source of livelihood here – needs education. You will be able to read the instructions on the chemicals to use in agriculture. Uneducated people are looked down upon in society. For instance, a common reaction to someone who has done something bad in the community, is: ‘Why do you act like someone who has no [school] education?’
The fact that our President went to school serves to show the importance of education and should be a source of inspiration for youth to go to school.

You will be able to speak with people from different social/ethnic backgrounds. For example, people who went to school are able to speak English, an international language. Also, s/he has good social and communication skills.
The government is encouraging people to go to school so that one might have a better life.
All: Most boys study up to form 4.
[And girls?] All: Most girls study up to form 4 but there are some who fail to reach or finish form 4 because of early marriages.
Boys and girls should be educated up to the point where he/she thinks it is enough for him/her to improve his/her well-being.
It varies with parents.

Most parents are more committed to send a boy child to school, than a girl child. Some parents think that a girl child will not look after them when she gets married. Other parents fear the risk of a girl child being pregnant, which amounts to having lost the money invested in the girl’s education.

Sheep are longer common because most people in this community are now going to church. Here, sheep are mostly used for traditional rituals, which the church discourages.
In the past, donkeys were used as a mode of transport but now there are a lot of cars.
Chickens are important because even the poorest have them. Chicken are used for family consumption and for sale.
Cattle are important because they are used as draught power, in our cultural practices for paying lobola and also provide manure.
No because currently any person can grow any crop in the fields. In families, men and women do agriculture jointly because they are growing for business.
There are some livestock types which are kept by men but not by women such as rabbits, pigs, sheep and donkeys. The rest of the livestock can be kept by either men or women.
Women can grow maize but they face difficulties because they do not have land to grow for themselves and they will not be able to find male labor where it is required.
Young men can grow groundnuts and sell on their own. However, it is not easy for a young man to grow groundnuts. Society will laugh at him because groundnuts is considered a woman’s crop.

The father is responsible for distributing the plots. The plots can be given to the son, daughter and mother depending on whether the land is available or not, and if there is need for allocating the land. The father has the powers to decide who farms which plot, or whether the plot can be farmed, or not.
When the father allocates plots he considers the quality of the field [soil] and who is getting the plot. Young women are usually given a small piece of land to grow groundnuts.
But in XX the decisions are jointly made by the father and the mother although the father has the final say.
It is rare for the husband to work in the wife’s plot but children usually work on the plots cultivated by the woman.
First we work in the fields designated for the family, which usually belongs to the male head, that is, the father/husband. Most of the household members work in the father’s field.
Most of the women’s plots are for groundnuts so they frequently go to the father’s plot where there is maize, the food crop.
They can hire labor from people in the community to work for pay.
Other things which can interfere with farming responsibilities are funerals and caring for sick household members.

[In general, is the right kind of labor available for agricultural activities when needed? How do [men] obtain additional labor when needed - in or outside the household?] In general, there is inadequate labor for agricultural activities in this community. People will hire additional labor from other people in the community and pay with money while others who do not have cash to pay will cultivate plots which they can manage.
How do female-headed households go about obtaining adult male labor when they need it during the rainy season?]
Female headed households can hire male labor to work for them and pay with chickens and maize grain.
If married she consults her husband. In this ward we do not have single women who have their own plots because they are under the authority of their parents.

If married he consults his wife and if not married he consult his parents.
